questions.instruction: One of these emails is a phishing attempt. Can you spot the red flags?
questions.teaching_point: Look for mismatched sender domains, generic greetings, and suspicious HTTP links with high urgency.

headers.subject: URGENT: Your account will be suspended!

body.content:
Dear Customer,

We were unable to process your last payment. To avoid service interruption, you must update your payment details immediately.
Failure to do so within 24 hours will result in permanent account cancellation.

clues.label: Sender Address
clues.explanation: Netflix would use a @netflix.com domain, not a free @gmail.com address.

clues.label: Generic Greeting
clues.explanation: The use of 'Dear Customer' instead of your actual name is a common sign of mass phishing.

clues.label: Suspicious Link
clues.explanation: The link uses 'http' instead of 'https' and points to a non-official domain.

emails.explanation: This is a classic phishing email. It uses a free email provider, a generic greeting, a non-secure link, and extreme urgency to pressure the user.

headers.subject: A quick update regarding your membership

body.content:
Hi Alex,

We're having some trouble with your current payment method. Please check your account settings to ensure your information is up to date.

clues.label: Sender Domain
clues.explanation: The email comes from a verified netflix.com subdomain.

clues.label: Personalization
clues.explanation: The email addresses the user by their actual name.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate email. It uses a professional tone, personalized greeting, and links directly to the official secure Netflix domain.

questions.instruction: Compare these two Amazon emails. Which one is trying to trick you?
questions.teaching_point: Be wary of 'look-alike' domains that look correct at a glance but contain subtle changes.

body.content:
Hello,

We detected an unusual sign-in attempt to your Amazon account from a new device in Singapore. If this was not you, please secure your account immediately to prevent unauthorized purchases.

clues.label: Domain Inspection
clues.explanation: The domain 'amazon-security-check.com' is not amazon.com. Attackers often add words like 'security' or 'verify' to make fake domains look official.

emails.explanation: This is a medium-difficulty phish. The branding is professional and the tone is helpful, but the sender address and the link lead to a fake domain created to mimic Amazon.

body.content:
Hi Alex,

Good news! Your package is on its way. You can track your delivery using the button below.

clues.label: Official Domain
clues.explanation: The sender and the link both point directly to the legitimate amazon.com domain.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate transactional email with a correct sender address and a secure, official link.

questions.instruction: These emails look almost identical. Only a very careful check will reveal the fake.
questions.teaching_point: High-level phishing uses perfect branding and personalized context. Always inspect the actual domain and headers carefully.

headers.subject: Mandatory Action: 2024 Remote Work Policy Update

body.content:
Dear Alex,

As part of our annual compliance review, all employees are required to review and digitally sign the updated 2024 Remote Work Policy. Please complete this by the end of the week to ensure your remote access privileges remain active.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

IT Service Desk
Global Operations

clues.label: Subtle Domain Shift
clues.explanation: The corporate domain is 'company.com', but the sender is using 'company-global-it.com'. This is a sophisticated look-alike domain designed to blend in with corporate jargon.

clues.label: Link Destination
clues.explanation: The link points to 'company-policy-portal.com' instead of the internal company intranet.

emails.explanation: This is a hard phish. It uses professional corporate tone, correct naming, and a plausible scenario. The only way to detect it is to notice that the domain is slightly different from the official company domain.

body.content:
Hi Alex,

The updated 2024 Employee Handbook is now available for viewing on the corporate intranet. Please take a moment to read through the changes regarding benefits and leave.

clues.label: Internal Domain
clues.explanation: The email originates from the official 'company.com' domain and links to an internal 'intranet.company.com' subdomain.

emails.explanation: This is a legitimate internal communication. The sender and the destination link both belong to the official company domain.
